newsitem.title: USA: Texas Water Board plans $100 mln in July sales.
newsitem.headline: Texas Water Board plans $100 mln in July sales.

text.p: The Texas Water Development Board plans to sell three series of bonds totaling $100 million in late July, the board's debt issuance manager said Monday.
Debt Issuance Manager Nancy Banks Marstiller said $75 million of the bonds will be used for its ongoing water supply program, which lends money to local municipalities to build Vwater projects.

The remaining $25 million will be split into $15 million for the board's economically distressed areas' water supply program and $10 million for economically distressed areas' water quality enhancement program. Certain counties along the Texas-Mexico border can apply for those monies, she said.

The bonds will be sold through negotiation, with Banc One Capital Corporation serving as senior manager. Artemis Capital Group Inc, Bear Stearns & Co, Legg Mason Wood Walker Inc, and Walton Johnson & Co will serve as co-managers.

The Water Development Board must still approve the preliminary official statement and bond resolutions before the sales can proceed. Approval from the Texas Bond Review Board approval is also needed, she said.
"So both of those are queued up for mid-July so we can make our scheduled deadline to sell at the end of July," Marstiller said.
